name: Smith Machine Romanian Deadlift
description: The Smith machine Romanian deadlift uses the guided bar path of the Smith machine to perform the hip hinge pattern. The fixed vertical track removes the need for lateral bar control, allowing the lifter to focus entirely on the hinge mechanics and hamstring stretch. It is a good option for beginners learning the RDL pattern or for those who want to train without a spotter on a hinge movement.

execution.starting_position: Set the Smith machine bar at hip height. Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding the bar with an overhand grip slightly outside hip width.
execution.setup_instructions: Rotate the bar to unlock it. Stand close to the bar with it at your upper thighs.
steps: Step 1: Brace the core, retract the shoulder blades, and push the hips back.
Step 2: Lower the bar along the front of the thighs in a straight path, keeping the bar close.
Step 3: Descend until a strong stretch is felt in the hamstrings, maintaining a neutral spine.
Step 4: Drive the hips forward to return to standing, squeezing the glutes at the top.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale and brace before the descent. Exhale as you drive up.
common_mistakes: Lower back rounding to gain additional depth
Bar drifting away from the legs
Knees bending too much, turning it into a deadlift
safety_considerations: The Smith machine's fixed path is vertical — ensure your hinge pattern matches this for natural movement
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Descend to mid-shin or as far as hamstring flexibility allows without spinal flexion.
coaching_cues: Push the hips back, not down
